newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cathay cargo load up 7.0 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Cathay cargo load up 7.0 pct in 1996.

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd said on Wednesday its cargo division carried 568,000 tonnes of cargo in 1996, up 7.0 percent from the previous year.

Cargo revenue tonne kilometres rose 14.0 percent against a rise of 15.9 percent in cargo capacity but cargo and mail load factors decreased marginally to 66.9 percent, the Hong Kong flag carrier said in a statement.

"Yields faced enormous downward pressure on almost all routes at the beginning of the year, but we were able to counter that with a rate increase in the latter part of the year," said James Barrington, Cathay Pacific's general manager, cargo.
"If yields can be maintained the cargo side of the airline looks very promising in 1997," he added.
Barrington said costs were under control and load factors continued to be high. "However, competition is intense, and we cannot afford to become complacent," he added.
Cathay Pacific said its cargo capacity increased significantly last year due to the replacement of L1011 TriStars with larger Airbus Industrie A330-300s and A340-300s, which have more cargo space.
Cathay Pacific launched a new freighter service to New York in 1996 and overall capacity was expected to increase by more than 2.8 percent in 1997, it said.

Cathay Pacific earlier announced that its cargo division posted turnover of HK$6.11 billion in 1996, up 5.6 percent from 1995. This represents about 20.5 percent of Cathay Pacific's total traffic turnover last year, it said.
